historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Histamine H2-receptor antagonists

starting.description: Histamine stimulated gastric acid secretion, but the antihistamines then available did not block that response despite blocking other histamine effects. This observed pharmacological distinction motivated a search for a second receptor antagonist using histamine analogues.

inspiration.description: Histamine and its observed gastric versus conventional-antihistamine-sensitive effects opened the program; selective and partial-agonist effects of synthetic histamine analogues supplied subsequent development clues.

steps.description: Observed histamine-induced acid secretion was resistant to existing antihistamines, motivating a search for a selective antagonist using analogues of histamine.
The team used selective agonist activity and an assay-revealed partial agonist to guide further histamine-analogue modifications.
Further changes produced a weak antagonist, then burimamide; later changes produced metiamide and cimetidine.
A later development series tested structural relatives of known H2 antagonists after prior active amidine results; its 2-guanidinothiazole sulfamoyl amidine compound 2e was famotidine.

design.description: Researchers deliberately synthesized and assayed histamine analogues, refined assays to detect partial antagonism, and modified side chains and terminal groups to improve antagonism and later potency and absorption. A later program explored chemically distinct H2-antagonist amidines, including the thiazole-containing sulfamoyl amidine famotidine.

circumstances.description: The receptor-directed program and histamine-analogue search were deliberate; this does not characterize every individual finding as expected.

limits: The founding histamine-derived series is established by discoverer accounts. Famotidine is a later, chemically distinct thiazole-containing H2 antagonist; the 1987 experimental paper does not establish it as a direct synthetic derivative of cimetidine.
conflicts: Bibliographic discrepancy, not a historical disagreement: Nature/PubMed list the 1972 report's coauthors as C. J. Durant and E. M. Parsons; a participant review cites the same paper as G. J. Durant and M. E. Parsons. The original printed byline was not inspected. The DOI and PMID identify the report; see the receipt for an additional conflated 1949 citation.
gaps: The full 1972 founding antagonist report was not read, only its one-sentence publisher abstract and metadata. The original 1964 proposal was not separately read beyond its reproduction in S2. The 1949 Ashford antihistamine study was located but not read in full. The separate 1984 paper preceding the famotidine series was located and read only at abstract extent; its role is reported in the 1987 paper.
